To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every material point. It also presents those departures as settled ("FINAL", "settled at principal level", "market standard"). We have no record of any such settlement. Under playbook §0.4/§6.3 we should treat the package as an opening position, not an agreed bargain.

Several Seller positions are also contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter, which gives us useful leverage.

---

## 1. Threshold points: framing and process

**The "FINAL / agreed at principal level" assertion.** Nothing in our authority process records principal-level agreement on any of these terms. In particular, Amelia Frost has given no written authority for the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks. The "market context" preamble is the counterparty's advocacy, not a source of authority. Our response should say plainly that we do not accept that any position is agreed or closed.

**Stale record.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026, so the record is about six weeks old. Before relying on any of the disclosed facts, we should ask for a bring-down covering:
- Bluefen consent status
- the Riverlark balance
- the Ironquay payment
- the DD-006 investigation
- the Sandbar renewals

**Drafting gap.** The Disclosure Letter jumps from [1.2] to [1.4]. We should ask whether a paragraph 1.3 exists or was removed, and require the final letter to be complete and consecutively numbered.

---

## 2. Liability regime

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this draft | **Reject.** The figure matches our fallback, but no authority has been given. A matching number is not clearance. Hold at 25%. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject.** Five times our position. At AUD 25k, many genuine claims would be excluded entirely. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded (tipping) | **Reject both limbs.** Five times our figure, plus a deductible structure that permanently absorbs the first AUD 250k of loss. Together with the de minimis, this materially erodes warranty protection. |
| **General claims period (cl 12.3)** | 18 months | 24 months. 18 months only with Amelia Frost's written approval | **Reject.** No approval given. |
| **"Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13)** | Blanket application | Categories kept separate. No hidden general-regime override | **Reject.** This would silently extend general caps, thresholds and time limits to Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants. Invert the default: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly stated. |
| **Fundamental / Title** | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | **Reject.** "Administrative simplicity" is no justification. Title and capacity go to the core of what we are buying. |
| **Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)** | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of them, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable | **Reject.** As drafted, this would purport to cap or bar fraud claims. Insert an express carve-out across caps, baskets, de minimis, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. This is a non-negotiable point. |

---

## 3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**General disclosure (DL [1.1]–[1.2]; Sched 7).** The Seller discloses the whole data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". This is the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure the playbook rejects.

- **Push back:** delete [1.1] and [1.2]. Disclosure should count only where it is specific and fair, identifying the matter with enough detail for the Buyer to assess its nature and scope, and cross-referenced to the relevant warranty.

**Non-admission ([1.4]).** A standard non-admission clause is acceptable in principle. However, it should not dilute the specific disclosures that follow, such as the express statement that the Bluefen consent is *not* in hand.

**Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** The Seller bars claims for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

- This doubles as a back-door general disclosure. It is a blanket knowledge exclusion that extends even to constructive knowledge.
- **Push back:** delete it. If any qualifier survives, it must:
  - be limited to actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons, after reasonable enquiry (the Seller-side qualifier the playbook permits);
  - never excuse claims for title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

---

## 4. Specific deal issues

**Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)**
- Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m, DD-002). The Seller offers reasonable endeavours and treats the condition as satisfied on mere delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- The Seller's own DL §2 confirms that no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions exists.
- **Push back:** the Completion condition must be:
  - an effective consent under clause 11.2; and
  - evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion.
- Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are both inadequate for a customer of this materiality.

**Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)**
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding (DD-003), with change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. The Seller offers a post-Completion release. DL §3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge exists.
- **Push back:** require:
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds;
  - executed security releases delivered at Completion.
- A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark plus Amelia Frost's approval. We have neither.
- Also confirm the ~AUD 3.2m is a current figure and is treated as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.

**Employee bonuses (funds flow)**
- The Seller says the DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) "are a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. DL §5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- This is precisely the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits. If the Seller does not pay these, they land on the Company, and therefore on us.
- **Push back:** require one of:
  - a specific funds-flow line item (AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs) paid at Completion; or
  - treatment as Debt/transaction expense deducted from price, with a supporting indemnity for any shortfall or later-triggered amount.

**Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)**
- The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment.
- DD-004 cl 7.3 makes the transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but as DL §4 itself notes, this is not bank-verified, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- The risk is broader than one payment: it extends to ownership of the IP.
- **Push back:** broaden the indemnity to cover:
  - any failure of the Company to own or have the right to use the SOW3 Project Materials;
  - third-party claims; and
  - costs of procuring assignment.
- Preserve the SOW3 cure: payment of outstanding fees plus delivery of a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a pre-Completion deliverable.
- Treat AUD 180,000 as unverified in both directions. Seek bank evidence and do not assume it is owed or paid.

**DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sched 6)**
- The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". DL §6 confirms that access, scope and any notification obligation are all unestablished. Up to ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) went to an unintended external address.
- We should neither accept the "immaterial" characterisation nor overstate the matter. There is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss.
- **Push back:** require:
  - log preservation and a completed investigation (ideally independent);
  - regular updates to Completion;
  - Buyer consultation before any regulator or individual notification decision;
  - a specific indemnity or an express carve-out from the general limitations for losses arising from the incident.
- Do not put a number on it.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- The Seller says these are ordinary course. DL §8 says the disclosure "does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course" and asks that DD-008 and DD-011 be read together.
- **Assess, don't assume.** Request the three contracts and timing analysis. Classify them (accrued liability, Debt, working capital or genuinely ordinary course) once the facts are in. No automatic Debt treatment or price deduction on our side, and no acceptance of the Seller's label either.

**Tax / IP**
- The Seller claims these are "settled under the general regime". They are not settled; both remain OPEN.
- Reject folding them into the general regime by default (see the "all Claims" override above). Reserve our position on cap and period, without assuming unlimited liability on either side.

**Title**
- The Seller relies solely on the DD-012 share register. DL §10 itself concedes that this is the source relied on, not Buyer verification. An internal register is not independent proof.
- **Push back:** require independent evidence:
  - ASIC company extract and share structure history;
  - original share certificates and transfer history;
  - PPSR searches showing no encumbrances over the shares;
  - Seller constitutional documents and board approvals evidencing authority and capacity.
- Title warranties must sit in the Fundamental regime (see section 2).

**Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- The DL says these involve a notification obligation and an assignment restriction respectively, and states that neither requires consent for a share sale.
- These are the Seller's characterisations. Have our team confirm by reviewing the change-of-control and assignment provisions directly, and diarise the lease notification as a Completion or post-Completion action.

---

## 5. Leverage

The Disclosure Letter undercuts the cover note on Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay and DD-006. The Seller cannot credibly maintain that these matters are resolved or immaterial while its own disclosures confirm they are open. Where the gap is clear, cite the DL paragraph directly in our mark-up.

---

## 6. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / agreed / market standard" framing.** Respond that no term is agreed and that we hold no principal-level authority for any fallback.
2. **Cap:** hold 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not move to 20% without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft.
3. **Thresholds:** AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 tipping basket. Reject AUD 25k/250k and the deductible structure.
4. **Claims period:** 24 months. Reject 18 months absent Amelia Frost's written approval.
5. **Fundamental/Title:** separate regime with a 100% cap, at least 6 years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
6. **Fraud carve-out** from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-negotiable.
7. **Delete the "applies to all Claims" override.** Keep Title, Tax, IP, indemnities, payment and covenant claims separate.
8. **Disclosure:** strike general data-room and public-record disclosure. Specific and fair disclosure only.
9. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl 8.3. Any qualifier should be limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and never applied to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
10. **Bluefen:** effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a pre-Completion condition.
11. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and releases at Completion. Post-Completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval.
12. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, backed by an indemnity.
13. **Ironquay:** broadened IP indemnity, SOW3 cure preserved, AUD 180,000 bank-verified.
14. **DD-006:** preservation, investigation, updates and consultation rights, plus specific protection. No assumed breach or quantum.
15. **Sandbar:** obtain contracts and classify on the facts. No automatic treatment either way.
16. **Tax/IP:** mark as OPEN. Reject "settled under the general regime".
17. **Title:** require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence beyond DD-012.
18. **Process:** request a bring-down of the 22 September record, explain the missing DL [1.3], and verify the lease and Mossvale characterisations ourselves.

Any move to a fallback position (items 2, 4 and 11) should go to Amelia Frost for written authority before it is conveyed to the Seller.
